# Servo positioning -- OpenPLC starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The program's logic section is yours.*

**The task.** Shuttle the axis between station A at 100 mm and station B, the panel's pot, dwelling a second at each, from Start until Stop. The drive does nothing until axis.enable has been on long enough for axis.ready, and every move needs axis.velocity as well as axis.target. When the drive faults it stops itself and latches axis.error: hold your sequence, show it, and acknowledge -- a rising edge of axis.ack -- only when the operator presses Reset and axis.fault has gone.

**Done when.** The carriage stops on A and on B in turn, and on the new B as soon as you turn the pot. Raise axis.fault mid-move and the carriage quick-stops; clear it, and nothing moves until somebody presses Reset -- a program that acknowledges on its own is automatic restart by another name. Careful with inposition: on the scan that writes a new target it still describes the old one, so arrive on axis.position against the station you are going to.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`servo_positioning.st`](servo_positioning.st) | Every I/O point declared at its located address, with an empty logic section. |
| [`mbconfig.cfg`](mbconfig.cfg) | The Slave Device entry that points OpenPLC's Modbus master at the sidecar. |

The walkthrough for OpenPLC itself -- installing, compiling, timing,
troubleshooting -- is [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md). This page
is only what is different about this scene.

## Run it

1. Open the scene in FactoryForge: pick "Servo positioning" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/servo_positioning.json).
2. **Then** start the sidecar as the Modbus slave. The order matters: the
   addresses below are the ones it hands out for this scene's tags, and a
   sidecar that was already running when you changed scene keeps its old
   addresses and puts the new tags above them.

   In the folder FactoryForge was extracted to:

   ```
   .\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp -o port 5502
   ```

   On Linux it is `./factoryforge-sidecar`. If OpenPLC runs in WSL or a VM, add
   `-o host <the address it reaches this machine on>` and read the warning
   it prints. Check the address map it prints against the table below.

   <!-- from-source -->
   (From a source checkout: `python -m factoryforge_sidecar connect ...`
   in `sidecar/`, in place of the command above.)
   <!-- /from-source -->
3. Compile `servo_positioning.st` in OpenPLC (web UI *Programs -> Upload*, or copy it
   into `webserver/st_files/` and run `./scripts/compile_program.sh servo_positioning.st`)
   and copy `mbconfig.cfg` to `webserver/core/`,
   or enter these numbers in *Slave Devices -> Add new device*
   (Generic Modbus TCP device, port 5502, slave id 1):

| Block | Start | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Discrete Inputs (%IX100.0) | 0 | 8 |
| Coils (%QX100.0) | 0 | 7 |
| Input Registers (%IW100) | 0 | 4 |
| Holding Registers - Read (%IW100) | 0 | 0 |
| Holding Registers - Write (%QW100) | 0 | 6 |

4. Start the PLC. To have it marked instead, run the grader in place of the
   3D scene -- same tags, same addresses. Stop the sidecar (Ctrl+C) first,
   then start the grader in one terminal:

   ```
   .\factoryforge-sidecar grade --scene servo-positioning
   ```

   and, in a second terminal, the sidecar with the bus port the grader
   printed:

   ```
   .\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp --port <bus port it printed> -o port 5502
   ```

   (`./factoryforge-sidecar` on Linux, in both.)

## I/O

`PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp); `PLC reads` is an input
(a sensor, a button, a measurement). *Brief* marks the signals the task names;
the rest are there to be used, such as each drive's fault contact. Modbus
addresses are decimal, as the sidecar prints them: `0x10` is coil ten.

| Tag | Direction | Type | Modbus | In the program | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `axis.ack` | PLC writes | bit | 0x0 | `AxisAck` %QX100.0 | acknowledge a latched error: RISING edge, and only once its cause has gone | yes |
| `axis.enable` | PLC writes | bit | 0x1 | `AxisEnable` %QX100.1 | power the drive (a level, like MC_Power.Enable) | yes |
| `axis.error` | PLC reads | bit | 1x0 | `AxisError` %IX100.0 | latched drive error: the axis has stopped itself and waits for an acknowledge | yes |
| `axis.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x1 | `AxisFault` %IX100.1 | drive fault present: TRUE = the cause of an error is still there | yes |
| `axis.inposition` | PLC reads | bit | 1x2 | `AxisInposition` %IX100.2 | stopped within 0.5 mm of the target it holds NOW -- stale on the scan you change the target | yes |
| `axis.position` | PLC reads | float | 3x0 + 3x1 | `AxisPositionHi` %IW100 + `AxisPositionLo` %IW101 -> `AxisPosition` : REAL | actual position, mm | yes |
| `axis.ready` | PLC reads | bit | 1x3 | `AxisReady` %IX100.3 | powered and error-free | yes |
| `axis.target` | PLC writes | float | 4x0 + 4x1 | `AxisTargetHi` %QW100 + `AxisTargetLo` %QW101 -> `AxisTarget` : REAL | target position, mm, 0..1000 | yes |
| `axis.velocity` | PLC writes | float | 4x2 + 4x3 | `AxisVelocityHi` %QW102 + `AxisVelocityLo` %QW103 -> `AxisVelocity` : REAL | move velocity, mm/s (the axis caps it at 500) | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x4 | `PanelEstop` %IX100.4 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x2 | `PanelGreen` %QX100.2 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x3 | `PanelRed` %QX100.3 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | bit | 1x5 | `PanelReset` %IX100.5 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | float | 3x2 + 3x3 | `PanelSetpointHi` %IW102 + `PanelSetpointLo` %IW103 -> `PanelSetpoint` : REAL | the operator's pot, 300..950 mm (starts at 800) | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | bit | 1x6 | `PanelStart` %IX100.6 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x7 | `PanelStop` %IX100.7 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `position_display.value` | PLC writes | int | 4x4 + 4x5 | `PositionDisplayValueHi` %QW104 + `PositionDisplayValueLo` %QW105 -> `PositionDisplayValue` : DINT | number shown on the display (mm) | yes |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x4 | `TowerGreen` %QX100.4 | tower lamp, green | yes |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x5 | `TowerRed` %QX100.5 | tower lamp, red | yes |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | bit | 0x6 | `TowerYellow` %QX100.6 | tower lamp, yellow | yes |

## Four things this scene's wiring does not forgive

- **A 32-bit value is two registers**, high word first. This scene has 5:
  `axis.position`, `axis.target`, `axis.velocity`, `panel.setpoint`,
  `position_display.value`. The program's first and last sections move them
  between the registers and plain DINT/REAL variables, so your logic never
  sees a register. OpenPLC's `DWORD_TO_REAL` converts the *number*
  (`16#3F800000` becomes 1065353216.0, not 1.0), so the starter rebuilds a
  REAL bit by bit instead. [`../check_starters.sh`](../check_starters.sh)
  compiles the helpers with OpenPLC's own matiec and checks them against two
  million bit patterns.
- **Anything polled can be missed if it is short.** OpenPLC's master reads
  every 50 ms. A button click in the 3D scene holds its tag for 0.2 s (the
  panel's Press Hold setting) and then leaves it off for at least as long, so
  every click is read several times: act on its rising edge, not its level.
  The grader holds each press for 0.15 s. The same goes the other way: hold an
  output you want the scene to see for well over one polling period.
- **An output you never write is FALSE.** The master rewrites the whole coil
  block on every poll, including coils your program does not touch.
- **Every input reads FALSE until OpenPLC's first poll returns.** The runtime
  starts scanning before its Modbus master has read the slave, and
  `panel.estop` is normally closed, so for those first scans it looks struck.
  A trip latched on `NOT PanelEstop` then trips itself every time OpenPLC
  starts, and Start does nothing. Arm the trip only once the E-stop has read
  healthy (`IF PanelEstop THEN EstopSeen := TRUE; END_IF;` and trip on
  `EstopSeen AND NOT PanelEstop`), and keep refusing Start while it reads
  FALSE, so a cut wire still stops the line. The section 2 comment in the
  `.st` has the pattern;
  [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md#troubleshooting) says why.
